full_judgment:
Whether in the facts and on the circumstances of the case, the Appellate Tribunal, Chittagong Bench, Chittagong was legally justified in maintaining the order of the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes in confirming the reassessment made by the Extra-Assistant Commissioner of Taxes under section 83(2)/156/159/93(5) of the Ordinance, out of which the assessment under section 83(2) of the Extra-Assistant Commissioner of Taxes was annulled by the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes (Appeals) as well as the Appellate Tribunal, Chittagong Bench, Chittagong in Income Tax Appeal No. 3437 of 2000-01 dated 27-3-2001, that the assessment under section 83(2) of the Ordinance was barred by limitation, can the Appellate Tribunal of Chittagong Bench, Chittagong by its order dated 19-9-2002 without controverting the findings of its past order dated 27-3-2001 and confirm the order of the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes? 

 12. Secondly, he submitted that once the assessment was annulled on the ground of limitation, the Extra-Assistant Commissioner of Taxes has got no jurisdiction to reopen the assessment. 

 15. Thirdly, the setting aside, cancellation or annulment of the earlier assessment on the ground of limitation by the Appellate Tribunal appears to be ex-facie bad, illegal and unauthorised. Sub-section (2) of section 83 of the Ordinance requires of the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes to complete the assessment of the total income of an assessee within thirty days after the completion of the hearing and determine the sum payable by him on the basis of such assessment and communicate the order to the assessee within thirty days next following. But If he fails to do so that would not ipso facto entail any consequence to make his assessment set aside, cancelled or annulled for being beyond the period of said thirty days. Section 94 of course prohibits any assessment of any income after the expiry of the time specified therein however, subject to sub- sections (2) and (3). It is now well settled that section 83 prescribes the initial period of limitation while section 94 the last one. So, if the assessment that could not be made within thirty days of completion of the hearing under section 83(2) but completed before the expiry of the period prescribed by section 94 it would not be barred. 

 16. In the case at hand, the Appellate Additional Commissioner of Taxes by order dated 28-9- 2000 found that the hearing of the case before the Extra-Assistant Commissioner of Taxes was completed on 2-9-99. And the Extra-Assistant Commissioner of Taxes made the assessment of the total income on 8-5-2000 under section 83(2) of the Ordinance. Upon such findings, he set aside the assessment for being barred by limitation. The Taxes Appellate Tribunal also by its order dated 27- 3-2001 upheld such erroneous order.
